question: Should OpenClaw accept static SecretRefs in `sandbox.docker.env` when resolved values still become Docker/container environment variables visible to Docker operators and sandboxed processes?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but accepting it changes a credential delivery boundary and expands the supported SecretRef config surface.

options.title: Accept with explicit boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR only after maintainer/security review explicitly accepts SecretRef-backed Docker env metadata exposure and confirms docs/audit behavior are aligned.

options.title: Require stronger warning first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to explicitly call out SecretRef-backed Docker env exposure in user-facing docs before merge.

options.title: Reject env delivery for secrets
options.body: Pause or close the linked PR and design a non-env secret delivery path if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR only after maintainer/security review explicitly accepts SecretRef-backed Docker env metadata exposure and confirms docs/audit behavior are aligned.
